title: Most marathon runners at the 2017 IAAF World Championships were rearfoot strikers, and most did not change footstrike pattern
claims: Across 149 athletes in the 2017 IAAF World Championships marathons, more than 75% (115/149) kept a consistent footstrike pattern between laps, meaning fewer than one quarter changed pattern during the race.
Of 37 men classified as rearfoot strikers in lap 1, 34 (92%) maintained that pattern; of 32 men classified as non-rearfoot in lap 1, 21 (66%) maintained it.
In the women's marathon at the same championships, 57 of 78 finishers (73%) were rearfoot strikers, 19 (24%) midfoot and 2 (3%) forefoot during lap 4.
The results show that rearfoot striking is common even at world-championship level.
